pictures.subject: backdrop
pictures.name: The hills
pictures.prompt: Convert the entire image into a warm hand-painted storybook illustration in soft gouache, viewed directly from above, keeping every element exactly in its current position, shape and size, with the plain mid-grey padding bands above and below left as flat grey with no painting over them. The wooded limestone hills of a post-apocalyptic winter world, four years abandoned: paint the snow-covered hillside ground in layered gouache strokes of muted ivory, ash-blue and pale ochre, showing packed snow cracked open over limestone outcrops, frozen mud ruts along every path and road, shallow icy puddles catching dull winter light in the open clearings, and drifts banked against fences and rock edges. Every path and road stays exactly where it is but gains visible tyre tracks and boot-shaped depressions pressed into the snow, long since frozen and untouched. Fences become weathered split-timber or rusted wire, posts leaning slightly from frost-heave. The broad frozen pond or stream patch in the lower-centre becomes dark grey-green ice with white stress cracks radiating from the banks. Every tree stays exactly in place but becomes a real tree seen from above: dense snow-laden spruce and fir crowns painted as soft dark-green rosettes ringed with white, bare deciduous branches like ink-wash tangles dusted with frost, casting short blue-grey shadows across the snow beneath them in the low winter light. Rounded limestone boulders and rock outcrops keep their positions but gain warm stone colour, mossy ochre undersides and blue-white snow caps.

pictures.subject: backdrop
pictures.name: The Hidden Caves
pictures.prompt: Repaint the entire map panel (leaving the plain mid-grey bands above and below untouched) as a warm hand-painted gouache storybook illustration viewed from directly overhead, set inside the limestone cave system known as The Hidden Caves in the post-apocalyptic world of Doomsville — a natural underground refuge carved into a rocky hillside among pine forest, occupied by a lone survivor named Ben roughly four years after civilisation collapsed. Every element stays precisely in its current position, shape and size. The cave-floor ground between and around the stone-flagged passages becomes rough, hand-painted bare earth and limestone rubble — ochre, umber and cool grey — with visible brush texture, scattered grit, hairline cracks in the rock, dried mud pooling in low corners, and faint bootprint tracks pressed into the dusty soil. The dark blurred cave-dirt surround outside the flagged areas is painted as raw limestone cavern floor with visible strata lines, loose pebbles, patches of pale calcite and deep shadow fading toward the edges. The paved stone corridors and chamber floors keep their irregular flagstone layout but are rendered with gouache in warm ash-grey and blue-grey tones, individual stones shaded with subtle depth, mortar cracks picked out in dark umber, and small puddles of seepage water catching a faint amber glow from implied torch or lantern light somewhere off the map edge, casting soft warm pools across two or three flags. The large irregular chamber at upper-centre and the smaller chambers at left and upper-right become cave rooms with gently rounded rocky walls painted in layered warm stone tones, their edges ragged and organic.

The creek crossing sits where the roads meet — paint it as a low stone-and-concrete bridge, its parapet half-buried under packed snow, the frozen creek beneath rendered as dull blue-grey cracked ice with dark water glinting through fissures, the ice surface scarred with old footprints and drag marks.
